- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at +2–5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive (0.5–0.8), model frequently overreacts to short-term volatility; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.27–0.53), model often fails to capture downward pressure; add 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment if recent 5-day average is falling.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag; if true outcome is below 70.00, model often misses the dip; adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment is weak or price is trending down.
